DensityOptions#summary.en:
Options shared by the density / probability mass (`d*`) functions.
Corresponds to R's `log` argument.

DensityOptions.log#summary.en: If `true`, return the log of the density (or probability). Default `false`.

DistName#summary.en: Distributions known to {@link distSummary} (the names of their d/p/q/r functions).

DistSummary.kurtosis#summary.en: Excess kurtosis (0 for the normal distribution).

DistSummary.mean#summary.en: Mean (NaN when it does not exist, `Infinity` when it is infinite).

DistSummary.median#summary.en: Median: the q function at 0.5 (for discrete distributions the smallest x with F(x) >= 0.5).

DistSummary.mode#summary.en: Mode: the maximum of the density (NaN when it is not unique; the larger of two adjacent modes).

DistSummary.sd#summary.en: Standard deviation, the square root of the variance.

DistSummary.variance#summary.en: Variance (NaN when it does not exist, `Infinity` when it is infinite).

GammaParams#summary.en:
Parameters of the gamma distribution. Give either `rate` or `scale`; if both are given,
`scale` must equal `1 / rate`.

GammaParams.scale#summary.en: Scale. Default `1`. Do not combine with a different `rate`.

InvgammaParams#summary.en: Scale parameter of the inverse gamma distribution.

InvgammaParams.beta#summary.en: Scale (the rate of the gamma distribution of 1/X). Default `1`.

LaplaceParams#summary.en: Location and scale of the Laplace distribution.

LocationScaleParams#summary.en: Location and scale parameters, used by the logistic and Cauchy distributions.

LognormalParams#summary.en: Parameters of the log-normal distribution (mean and standard deviation on the log scale).

LognormalParams.meanlog#summary.en: Mean of the distribution on the log scale. Default `0`.

LognormalParams.sdlog#summary.en: Standard deviation of the distribution on the log scale. Default `1`.

MultinomialOptions.log#summary.en: If `true`, return the log probability. Default `false`.

MultinomialOptions.size#summary.en: Total number of objects; defaults to the sum of `x` (it must equal it, as in R).

NegBinomialParams#summary.en: Parameters of the negative binomial distribution. Give exactly one of `prob` and `mu`.

NegBinomialParams.mu#summary.en: Mean (`mu = size * (1 - prob) / prob`). Do not combine with `prob`.

NegBinomialParams.prob#summary.en: Probability of success on each trial (`0 < prob <= 1`). Do not combine with `mu`.

NoncentralOption#summary.en: Noncentrality option accepted by the chi-squared, t, F and beta distribution functions.

NoncentralOption.ncp#summary.en:
Noncentrality parameter. If omitted, the central distribution is used.
As in R, an explicit `ncp: 0` describes the same distribution as the central one. R then uses
the noncentral algorithm, so its values can differ slightly from the central values;
rStats.js returns values of the same accuracy in both cases.

NormalOptions.logP#summary.en: If `true`, probabilities are given (to `qnorm`) and returned (from `pnorm`) as log(p). Default `false`.

NormalOptions.lowerTail#summary.en: If `true`, probabilities are P[X <= x]; if `false`, P[X > x]. Default `true`.

ParetoParams#summary.en: Shape and scale of the Pareto distribution.

ParetoParams.b#summary.en: Scale (the lower limit of the support). Default `1`.

TailOptions#summary.en:
Options shared by the distribution (`p*`) and quantile (`q*`) functions.
Correspond to R's `lower.tail` and `log.p` arguments.

TailOptions.logP#summary.en: If `true`, probabilities are given (to `q*`) and returned (from `p*`) as log(p). Default `false`.

TailOptions.lowerTail#summary.en: If `true`, probabilities are P[X <= x]; if `false`, P[X > x]. Default `true`.

TriangParams#summary.en: Limits and mode of the triangular distribution.

TukeyOptions.logP#summary.en: If `true`, probabilities are given (to `q*`) and returned (from `p*`) as log(p). Default `false`.

TukeyOptions.lowerTail#summary.en: If `true`, probabilities are P[X <= x]; if `false`, P[X > x]. Default `true`.

TukeyOptions.nranges#summary.en: Number of groups whose ranges are compared; the statistic is the maximum of that many ranges. Default `1`.

VectorResult#summary.en:
Result type matching the shape of a {@link Vectorizable} input:
`number` for a number, `Float64Array` for a `Float64Array`, and `number[]` for an array.

Vectorizable#summary.en:
Input accepted as the vectorized first argument of the distribution functions
(the counterpart of R's automatic vectorization).
A number gives a number, a `number[]` gives a `number[]`, and a `Float64Array` gives a `Float64Array`.

WeibullParams#summary.en: Parameters of the Weibull distribution (besides the positional `shape`).

darcsine#@param x.en: Value(s) at which to evaluate: a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

darcsine#summary.en:
Density of the arcsine distribution on (a, b), f(x) = 1 / (pi sqrt((x - a)(b - x))).
Not an R function. Neither base R nor extraDistr has the arcsine distribution; this equals
`dbeta((x - a) / (b - a), 0.5, 0.5) / (b - a)`.

dbeta#@param x.en: Value(s) at which to evaluate: a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

dbeta#summary.en:
Density of the beta distribution. Equivalent to R's `dbeta(x, shape1, shape2, ncp = 0, log = FALSE)`.

If `ncp` is omitted the central distribution is used; otherwise the noncentral beta distribution.

dbinom#@param prob.en: Probability of success on each trial.

dbinom#@param x.en: Value(s) at which to evaluate: a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

dbinom#summary.en: Probability mass function of the binomial distribution. Equivalent to R's `dbinom(x, size, prob, log = FALSE)`.

dcauchy#@param x.en: Value(s) at which to evaluate: a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

dcauchy#summary.en: Density of the Cauchy distribution. Equivalent to R's `dcauchy(x, location = 0, scale = 1, log = FALSE)`.

dchisq#@param x.en: Value(s) at which to evaluate: a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

dchisq#summary.en:
Density of the chi-squared distribution. Equivalent to R's `dchisq(x, df, ncp = 0, log = FALSE)`.

If `ncp` is omitted the central distribution is used; otherwise the noncentral chi-squared distribution.

dexp#@param x.en: Value(s) at which to evaluate: a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

dexp#summary.en: Density of the exponential distribution. Equivalent to R's `dexp(x, rate = 1, log = FALSE)`.

df#@param x.en: Value(s) at which to evaluate: a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

df#summary.en:
Density of the F distribution. Equivalent to R's `df(x, df1, df2, ncp, log = FALSE)`.

If `ncp` is omitted the central distribution is used; otherwise the noncentral F distribution.

dgamma#@param x.en: Value(s) at which to evaluate: a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

dgamma#@throws.en: RangeError if both `rate` and `scale` are given and `scale` is not `1 / rate`.

dgamma#summary.en: Density of the gamma distribution. Equivalent to R's `dgamma(x, shape, rate = 1, scale = 1/rate, log = FALSE)`.

dgeom#@param prob.en: Probability of success on each trial.

dgeom#@param x.en: Value(s) at which to evaluate: a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

dgeom#summary.en: Probability mass function of the geometric distribution (number of failures before the first success). Equivalent to R's `dgeom(x, prob, log = FALSE)`.

dhyper#@param m.en: Number of white balls in the urn.

dhyper#@param n.en: Number of black balls in the urn.

dhyper#@param x.en: Value(s) at which to evaluate: a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

dhyper#summary.en: Probability mass function of the hypergeometric distribution (number of white balls among `k` drawn without replacement from an urn of `m` white and `n` black balls). Equivalent to R's `dhyper(x, m, n, k, log = FALSE)`.

dinvgamma#@param x.en: Value(s) at which to evaluate: a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

dinvgamma#summary.en:
Density of the inverse gamma distribution. Equivalent to `extraDistr::dinvgamma(x, alpha, beta = 1, log = FALSE)` in R.
f(x) = beta^alpha x^(-alpha-1) exp(-beta/x) / Gamma(alpha).

distSummary#summary.en:
Mean, variance, standard deviation, median, mode, skewness and excess kurtosis of a distribution, given by the
name of its d/p/q/r functions and their parameters (with the same names and defaults; `gamma` takes `rate` or
`scale`, `nbinom` takes `prob` or `mu`). Invalid parameters give NaN throughout. The distributions are the central
ones: `ncp` of `chisq`, `beta`, `t` and `f` is not taken (an unknown key, a RangeError).
Not an R function. R has no function for these summaries; the R references are closed forms checked against
numerical moments.

dkumar#@param x.en: Value(s) at which to evaluate: a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

dkumar#summary.en: Density of the Kumaraswamy distribution. Equivalent to `extraDistr::dkumar(x, a, b, log = FALSE)` in R.

dlaplace#@param x.en: Value(s) at which to evaluate: a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

dlaplace#summary.en: Density of the Laplace distribution. Equivalent to `extraDistr::dlaplace(x, mu = 0, sigma = 1, log = FALSE)` in R.

dlnorm#@param x.en: Value(s) at which to evaluate: a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

dlnorm#summary.en: Density of the log-normal distribution. Equivalent to R's `dlnorm(x, meanlog = 0, sdlog = 1, log = FALSE)`.

dlogis#@param x.en: Value(s) at which to evaluate: a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

dlogis#summary.en: Density of the logistic distribution. Equivalent to R's `dlogis(x, location = 0, scale = 1, log = FALSE)`.

dmultinom#@param prob.en: Category weights, K finite non-negative numbers, not all 0 (divided by their sum).

dmultinom#@param x.en: Counts, a vector of K non-negative integers.

dmultinom#@returns.en: The probability `N! / (x_1! ... x_K!) prod p_j^x_j` with `N = sum(x)`, or its log.

dmultinom#@throws.en:
RangeError if `x` and `prob` differ in length, `x` has a negative or non-integer value, `prob` has a
  negative or non-finite value or no positive value, or `size` differs from the sum of `x`.

dmultinom#summary.en:
Probability function of the multinomial distribution. Equivalent to R's
`dmultinom(x, size = NULL, prob, log = FALSE)`.

dnbinom#@param options.en: `prob` or `mu` (see {@link NegBinomialParams}; exactly one is required) and `log` (see {@link DensityOptions}).

dnbinom#@param size.en: Target number of successes (need not be an integer).

dnbinom#@param x.en: Value(s) at which to evaluate: a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

dnbinom#@throws.en: TypeError unless exactly one of `prob` and `mu` is given.

dnbinom#summary.en:
Probability mass function of the negative binomial distribution (number of failures before the `size`-th success). Equivalent to R's `dnbinom(x, size, prob, mu, log = FALSE)`.

The distribution is parameterized by `size` and exactly one of `prob` or `mu`. With `mu`, `size = Infinity` gives the Poisson distribution.

dnorm#@param x.en: Value(s) at which to evaluate: a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

dnorm#summary.en: Density of the normal distribution. Equivalent to R's `dnorm(x, mean = 0, sd = 1, log = FALSE)`.

dnorm.options.log#summary.en: If `true`, return the log density. Default `false`.

dpareto#@param x.en: Value(s) at which to evaluate: a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

dpareto#summary.en: Density of the Pareto distribution. Equivalent to `extraDistr::dpareto(x, a = 1, b = 1, log = FALSE)` in R.

dpois#@param x.en: Value(s) at which to evaluate: a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

dpois#summary.en: Probability mass function of the Poisson distribution. Equivalent to R's `dpois(x, lambda, log = FALSE)`.

dsignrank#@param x.en: Value(s) at which to evaluate: a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

dsignrank#@throws.en: RangeError if `n` is so large that the required table cannot be allocated.

dsignrank#summary.en: Probability mass function of the distribution of the Wilcoxon signed rank statistic. Equivalent to R's `dsignrank(x, n, log = FALSE)`.

dt#@param x.en: Value(s) at which to evaluate: a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

dt#summary.en:
Density of the t distribution. Equivalent to R's `dt(x, df, ncp, log = FALSE)`.

If `ncp` is omitted the central distribution is used; otherwise the noncentral t distribution.

As in R, `ncp: 0` gives the same values as the central distribution.

dtriang#@param x.en: Value(s) at which to evaluate: a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

dtriang#summary.en: Density of the triangular distribution. Equivalent to `extraDistr::dtriang(x, a = -1, b = 1, c = (a + b)/2, log = FALSE)` in R.

dunif#@param x.en: Value(s) at which to evaluate: a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

dunif#summary.en: Density of the uniform distribution. Equivalent to R's `dunif(x, min = 0, max = 1, log = FALSE)`.

dweibull#@param x.en: Value(s) at which to evaluate: a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

dweibull#summary.en: Density of the Weibull distribution. Equivalent to R's `dweibull(x, shape, scale = 1, log = FALSE)`.

dwilcox#@param x.en: Value(s) at which to evaluate: a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

dwilcox#@throws.en:
RangeError if `m` and `n` are so large that the required table cannot be allocated or would take more than
2^29 steps to build (min(m, n) times its length; about 6 to 8 s), or that the table loses its accuracy (near the
center for m = n >= 550 or so; the tails stay available).

dwilcox#summary.en:
Probability mass function of the distribution of the Wilcoxon rank sum statistic (Mann-Whitney U). Equivalent to R's `dwilcox(x, m, n, log = FALSE)`.

Unlike R, memory use grows only with the range of the statistic (at most `m * n / 2`), so large samples such as `m = n = 500` work.

parcsine#summary.en:
Distribution function of the arcsine distribution on (a, b): `pbeta((q - a) / (b - a), 0.5, 0.5)`.
Not an R function. Neither base R nor extraDistr has the arcsine distribution.

pbeta#@param q.en: Quantile(s): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

pbeta#summary.en:
Distribution function of the beta distribution. Equivalent to R's `pbeta(q, shape1, shape2, ncp = 0, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

If `ncp` is omitted the central distribution is used; otherwise the noncentral beta distribution.

pbinom#@param prob.en: Probability of success on each trial.

pbinom#@param q.en: Quantile(s): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

pbinom#summary.en: Distribution function of the binomial distribution. Equivalent to R's `pbinom(q, size, prob, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

pbvnorm#summary.en:
Probability that a standard bivariate normal pair (X, Y) with correlation `rho` lies in the rectangle
`lower ≤ (X, Y) ≤ upper`. Equivalent to `mvtnorm::pmvnorm()` in R. The same as
`pmvnorm(lower, upper, corr = matrix(c(1, rho, rho, 1), 2))`.
Bounds may be infinite. Accurate to about 1e-15 absolute.

pcauchy#@param q.en: Quantile(s): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

pcauchy#summary.en: Distribution function of the Cauchy distribution. Equivalent to R's `pcauchy(q, location = 0, scale = 1, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

pchisq#@param q.en: Quantile(s): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

pchisq#summary.en:
Distribution function of the chi-squared distribution. Equivalent to R's `pchisq(q, df, ncp = 0, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

If `ncp` is omitted the central distribution is used; otherwise the noncentral chi-squared distribution.

pexp#@param q.en: Quantile(s): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

pexp#summary.en: Distribution function of the exponential distribution. Equivalent to R's `pexp(q, rate = 1, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

pf#@param q.en: Quantile(s): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

pf#summary.en:
Distribution function of the F distribution. Equivalent to R's `pf(q, df1, df2, ncp, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

If `ncp` is omitted the central distribution is used; otherwise the noncentral F distribution.

pgamma#@param q.en: Quantile(s): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

pgamma#@throws.en: RangeError if both `rate` and `scale` are given and `scale` is not `1 / rate`.

pgamma#summary.en: Distribution function of the gamma distribution. Equivalent to R's `pgamma(q, shape, rate = 1, scale = 1/rate, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

pgeom#@param prob.en: Probability of success on each trial.

pgeom#@param q.en: Quantile(s): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

pgeom#summary.en: Distribution function of the geometric distribution (number of failures before the first success). Equivalent to R's `pgeom(q, prob, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

phyper#@param m.en: Number of white balls in the urn.

phyper#@param n.en: Number of black balls in the urn.

phyper#@param q.en: Quantile(s): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

phyper#summary.en: Distribution function of the hypergeometric distribution (number of white balls among `k` drawn without replacement from an urn of `m` white and `n` black balls). Equivalent to R's `phyper(q, m, n, k, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

pinvgamma#summary.en:
Distribution function of the inverse gamma distribution. Equivalent to
`extraDistr::pinvgamma(q, alpha, beta = 1, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)` in R.

pkumar#summary.en: Distribution function of the Kumaraswamy distribution. Equivalent to `extraDistr::pkumar(q, a, b, lower.tail, log.p)` in R.

plaplace#summary.en: Distribution function of the Laplace distribution. Equivalent to `extraDistr::plaplace(q, mu = 0, sigma = 1, lower.tail, log.p)` in R.

plnorm#@param q.en: Quantile(s): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

plnorm#summary.en: Distribution function of the log-normal distribution. Equivalent to R's `plnorm(q, meanlog = 0, sdlog = 1, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

plogis#@param q.en: Quantile(s): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

plogis#summary.en: Distribution function of the logistic distribution. Equivalent to R's `plogis(q, location = 0, scale = 1, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

pnbinom#@param options.en: `prob` or `mu` (see {@link NegBinomialParams}; exactly one is required), `lowerTail` and `logP` (see {@link TailOptions}).

pnbinom#@param q.en: Quantile(s): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

pnbinom#@param size.en: Target number of successes (need not be an integer).

pnbinom#@throws.en: TypeError unless exactly one of `prob` and `mu` is given.

pnbinom#summary.en:
Distribution function of the negative binomial distribution (number of failures before the `size`-th success). Equivalent to R's `pnbinom(q, size, prob, mu, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

The distribution is parameterized by `size` and exactly one of `prob` or `mu`. With `mu`, `size = Infinity` gives the Poisson distribution.

pnorm#@param q.en: Quantile(s): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

pnorm#summary.en:
Distribution function of the normal distribution.
Equivalent to R's `pnorm(q, mean = 0, sd = 1, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

ppareto#summary.en: Distribution function of the Pareto distribution. Equivalent to `extraDistr::ppareto(q, a = 1, b = 1, lower.tail, log.p)` in R.

ppois#@param q.en: Quantile(s): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

ppois#summary.en: Distribution function of the Poisson distribution. Equivalent to R's `ppois(q, lambda, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

psignrank#@param q.en: Quantile(s): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

psignrank#@throws.en: RangeError if `n` is so large that the required table cannot be allocated.

psignrank#summary.en: Distribution function of the distribution of the Wilcoxon signed rank statistic. Equivalent to R's `psignrank(q, n, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

pt#@param q.en: Quantile(s): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

pt#summary.en:
Distribution function of the t distribution. Equivalent to R's `pt(q, df, ncp, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

If `ncp` is omitted the central distribution is used; otherwise the noncentral t distribution.

ptriang#summary.en: Distribution function of the triangular distribution. Equivalent to `extraDistr::ptriang(q, a, b, c, lower.tail, log.p)` in R.

ptukey#@param df.en: Degrees of freedom of the standard deviation estimate.

ptukey#@param nmeans.en: Number of means (sample size of each range).

ptukey#@param q.en: Quantile(s): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

ptukey#summary.en:
Distribution function of the studentized range distribution (used by Tukey's HSD). Equivalent to R's `ptukey(q, nmeans, df, nranges = 1, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

Results aim at a relative accuracy of about 1e-15. R's `ptukey` is accurate to only about 8 digits, so values can differ from R's beyond that.

punif#@param q.en: Quantile(s): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

punif#summary.en: Distribution function of the uniform distribution. Equivalent to R's `punif(q, min = 0, max = 1, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

pweibull#@param q.en: Quantile(s): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

pweibull#summary.en: Distribution function of the Weibull distribution. Equivalent to R's `pweibull(q, shape, scale = 1, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

pwilcox#@param q.en: Quantile(s): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

pwilcox#@throws.en:
RangeError if `m` and `n` are so large that the required table cannot be allocated or would take more than
2^29 steps to build (min(m, n) times its length; about 6 to 8 s), or that the table loses its accuracy (near the
center for m = n >= 550 or so; the tails stay available).

pwilcox#summary.en:
Distribution function of the distribution of the Wilcoxon rank sum statistic (Mann-Whitney U). Equivalent to R's `pwilcox(q, m, n, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

Unlike R, memory use grows only with the range of the statistic (at most `m * n / 2`), so large samples such as `m = n = 500` work.

qarcsine#summary.en:
Quantile function of the arcsine distribution on (a, b): `a + (b - a) qbeta(p, 0.5, 0.5)`.
Not an R function. Neither base R nor extraDistr has the arcsine distribution.

qbeta#@param p.en: Probability (or log probability with `logP`): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

qbeta#summary.en:
Quantile function of the beta distribution. Equivalent to R's `qbeta(p, shape1, shape2, ncp = 0, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

If `ncp` is omitted the central distribution is used; otherwise the noncentral beta distribution.

qbinom#@param p.en: Probability (or log probability with `logP`): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

qbinom#@param prob.en: Probability of success on each trial.

qbinom#summary.en: Quantile function of the binomial distribution. Equivalent to R's `qbinom(p, size, prob, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

qcauchy#@param p.en: Probability (or log probability with `logP`): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

qcauchy#summary.en: Quantile function of the Cauchy distribution. Equivalent to R's `qcauchy(p, location = 0, scale = 1, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

qchisq#@param p.en: Probability (or log probability with `logP`): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

qchisq#summary.en:
Quantile function of the chi-squared distribution. Equivalent to R's `qchisq(p, df, ncp = 0, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

If `ncp` is omitted the central distribution is used; otherwise the noncentral chi-squared distribution.

qexp#@param p.en: Probability (or log probability with `logP`): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

qexp#summary.en: Quantile function of the exponential distribution. Equivalent to R's `qexp(p, rate = 1, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

qf#@param p.en: Probability (or log probability with `logP`): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

qf#summary.en:
Quantile function of the F distribution. Equivalent to R's `qf(p, df1, df2, ncp, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

If `ncp` is omitted the central distribution is used; otherwise the noncentral F distribution.

qgamma#@param p.en: Probability (or log probability with `logP`): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

qgamma#@throws.en: RangeError if both `rate` and `scale` are given and `scale` is not `1 / rate`.

qgamma#summary.en: Quantile function of the gamma distribution. Equivalent to R's `qgamma(p, shape, rate = 1, scale = 1/rate, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

qgeom#@param p.en: Probability (or log probability with `logP`): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

qgeom#@param prob.en: Probability of success on each trial.

qgeom#summary.en: Quantile function of the geometric distribution (number of failures before the first success). Equivalent to R's `qgeom(p, prob, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

qhyper#@param m.en: Number of white balls in the urn.

qhyper#@param n.en: Number of black balls in the urn.

qhyper#@param p.en: Probability (or log probability with `logP`): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

qhyper#summary.en: Quantile function of the hypergeometric distribution (number of white balls among `k` drawn without replacement from an urn of `m` white and `n` black balls). Equivalent to R's `qhyper(p, m, n, k, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

qinvgamma#summary.en:
Quantile function of the inverse gamma distribution. Equivalent to
`extraDistr::qinvgamma(p, alpha, beta = 1, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)` in R.

qkumar#summary.en: Quantile function of the Kumaraswamy distribution. Equivalent to `extraDistr::qkumar(p, a, b, lower.tail, log.p)` in R.

qlaplace#summary.en: Quantile function of the Laplace distribution. Equivalent to `extraDistr::qlaplace(p, mu = 0, sigma = 1, lower.tail, log.p)` in R.

qlnorm#@param p.en: Probability (or log probability with `logP`): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

qlnorm#summary.en: Quantile function of the log-normal distribution. Equivalent to R's `qlnorm(p, meanlog = 0, sdlog = 1, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

qlogis#@param p.en: Probability (or log probability with `logP`): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

qlogis#summary.en: Quantile function of the logistic distribution. Equivalent to R's `qlogis(p, location = 0, scale = 1, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

qnbinom#@param options.en: `prob` or `mu` (see {@link NegBinomialParams}; exactly one is required), `lowerTail` and `logP` (see {@link TailOptions}).

qnbinom#@param p.en: Probability (or log probability with `logP`): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

qnbinom#@param size.en: Target number of successes (need not be an integer).

qnbinom#@throws.en: TypeError unless exactly one of `prob` and `mu` is given.

qnbinom#summary.en:
Quantile function of the negative binomial distribution (number of failures before the `size`-th success). Equivalent to R's `qnbinom(p, size, prob, mu, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

The distribution is parameterized by `size` and exactly one of `prob` or `mu`. With `mu`, `size = Infinity` gives the Poisson distribution.

qnorm#@param p.en: Probability (or log probability with `logP`): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

qnorm#summary.en:
Quantile function of the normal distribution.
Equivalent to R's `qnorm(p, mean = 0, sd = 1, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

qpareto#summary.en: Quantile function of the Pareto distribution. Equivalent to `extraDistr::qpareto(p, a = 1, b = 1, lower.tail, log.p)` in R.

qpois#@param p.en: Probability (or log probability with `logP`): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

qpois#summary.en: Quantile function of the Poisson distribution. Equivalent to R's `qpois(p, lambda, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

qsignrank#@param p.en: Probability (or log probability with `logP`): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

qsignrank#@throws.en: RangeError if `n` is so large that the required table cannot be allocated.

qsignrank#summary.en: Quantile function of the distribution of the Wilcoxon signed rank statistic. Equivalent to R's `qsignrank(p, n, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

qt#@param p.en: Probability (or log probability with `logP`): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

qt#summary.en:
Quantile function of the t distribution. Equivalent to R's `qt(p, df, ncp, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

If `ncp` is omitted the central distribution is used; otherwise the noncentral t distribution.

qtriang#summary.en: Quantile function of the triangular distribution. Equivalent to `extraDistr::qtriang(p, a, b, c, lower.tail, log.p)` in R.

qtukey#@param df.en: Degrees of freedom of the standard deviation estimate.

qtukey#@param nmeans.en: Number of means (sample size of each range).

qtukey#@param p.en: Probability (or log probability with `logP`): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

qtukey#summary.en:
Quantile function of the studentized range distribution (used by Tukey's HSD). Equivalent to R's `qtukey(p, nmeans, df, nranges = 1, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

Results aim at a relative accuracy of about 1e-15. R's `ptukey` is accurate to only about 8 digits, so values can differ from R's beyond that.

qunif#@param p.en: Probability (or log probability with `logP`): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

qunif#summary.en: Quantile function of the uniform distribution. Equivalent to R's `qunif(p, min = 0, max = 1, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

qweibull#@param p.en: Probability (or log probability with `logP`): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

qweibull#summary.en: Quantile function of the Weibull distribution. Equivalent to R's `qweibull(p, shape, scale = 1, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

qwilcox#@param p.en: Probability (or log probability with `logP`): a number, `number[]` or `Float64Array`. The result has the same shape.

qwilcox#@throws.en:
RangeError if `m` and `n` are so large that the required table cannot be allocated or would take more than
2^29 steps to build (min(m, n) times its length; about 6 to 8 s), or that the table loses its accuracy (near the
center for m = n >= 550 or so; the tails stay available).

qwilcox#summary.en:
Quantile function of the distribution of the Wilcoxon rank sum statistic (Mann-Whitney U). Equivalent to R's `qwilcox(p, m, n, lower.tail = TRUE, log.p = FALSE)`.

Unlike R, memory use grows only with the range of the statistic (at most `m * n / 2`), so large samples such as `m = n = 500` work.
